pools-abo.note: two pools, three lanes, three message flows; written by the developer of the 2026-10-01 experiment, repaired in spike 2.26 (a parallel split without join)

pools-bestellung.note: three pools, five message flows, one from the first to the third pool; written by the developer of the 2026-10-01 experiment

pools-angebot.note: two pools without lanes; written by an LLM given only the task "customer asks a company for an offer, the company answers" and the rule "BPMN 2.0 XML without coordinates"

pools-bewerbung.note: two pools without lanes; written by an LLM given only the task "an applicant applies, the company invites or declines" and the rule

pools-wasserschaden.note: three pools without lanes; written by an LLM given only the task "a tenant reports water damage, the management commissions a craftsman who repairs it and sends an invoice" and the rule

blackbox-kredit.note: a bank with a black box on top (customer) and one below (credit agency), five message flows at their frames; written by an LLM given only the task "a bank handles a loan application, asks a credit agency, the customer gets an offer or a refusal; how customer and agency work inside is unknown" and the rule "BPMN 2.0 XML without coordinates"

blackbox-reklamation.note: a shop with two lanes and a black box on top (customer), four message flows at its frame; written by an LLM given only the task "an online shop handles a complaint, the customer gets a replacement or a credit note; how the customer works inside is unknown" and the rule

blackbox-werkstatt.note: a garage with a black box on top (customer) and one below (wholesaler), six message flows at their frames; written by an LLM given only the task "a garage takes a repair order, waits for the customer's approval of the estimate, orders parts from a wholesaler, repairs and reports; how customer and wholesaler work inside is unknown" and the rule

demo-angeheftet.note: two boundary events on one task (a timer that interrupts, an escalation that does not), an error on a collapsed sub-process beside its marker, an error whose flow goes back into its own service task

angeheftet-rechnung.note: an interrupting timer on a waiting task whose way leads through a decision back before its host; written by an LLM given only the task "a craftsman's office sends an invoice, accounting waits for the payment, after 14 days without it sends a reminder and waits again, after the second reminder hands the case to a collection agency" and the rule "BPMN 2.0 XML without coordinates"

angeheftet-antrag.note: an error on a service task whose way goes to a lane above, and a non-interrupting timer on a user task; written by an LLM given only the task "an authority checks an application automatically, by hand after a technical error, decides and sends the notice; after three days of deciding a reminder goes to the team lead without interrupting" and the rule

angeheftet-stoerung.note: a non-interrupting timer and an interrupting error on one collapsed sub-process (its content added for the lint, start and end were missing); written by an LLM given only the task "IT support classifies a fault and fixes it in a sub-process; after four hours the customer is told without interrupting; when hardware must be replaced the fix is broken off and a technician sent" and the rule

demo-angeheftet-bahnen.note: boundary events whose ways go into a lane below and a lane above, the latter in a row of its own facing the host's lane (review of 2.30, R7)

notiz-morgen.note: Ben's morgenroutine written anew, small and lint-clean: three lanes, a parallel split and join, a signal thrown and caught; its three text annotations at a manual task, at a throw event with a label and at the last task of a lane

notiz-zwei.note: two text annotations at one task, a long one at a gateway with a label, one at a task with a loop marker, one at an end event in another lane

notiz-fluss.note: text annotations at sequence flows: a short horizontal one, a vertical one with a label, one between lanes

notiz-pool.note: a text annotation at a pool, at a black box and at a message flow, in the collaboration, and one at a task in a process

notiz-r12.note: r12 with a boundary event: text annotations at a task, at a flow back with a long label and at the boundary event with a long label; one of them finds no free place near and goes to the border of its lane, which grows

demo-notizen.note: the demo text's section on text annotations: at a task (two), at a boundary event, at a sequence flow, at a message flow, at a pool and at a black box; one without text and one without an association left out

notiz-hund2.note: hund2 with four text annotations, one at a boundary event; where no round has a free place, the stripe's place with the fewest faults is taken, below the lane first at a boundary event (review of 2.31)

notiz-bauantrag.note: two pools, nine long text annotations, written by an LLM given only the task of a building application and the rule; stripes with the fewest faults, and text annotations that move with the lower pool when the upper one grows in the frame step (shift(); review of 2.31)

daten-geteilt.note: three lanes; one data object written in the first lane and read in the second and third, one shape in the lane nearest to all its users; a second one written and read across two lanes

daten-lesen-schreiben.note: one process without lanes; one task reads and writes the same data object (two lines 12 px apart), others read or write one each

daten-speicher.note: two lanes; a data store (50 × 50) read in one lane and written in the other, a data object between two lanes

daten-ereignis.note: data at a message start event, a throw and a catch event, an end event (a data store) and a boundary event, whose data object a task reads too

daten-viele.note: one task reading three references (two data stores) and writing a fourth; two references of one data object with the states "Entwurf" and "freigegeben", each a second line under the name

daten-eng.note: a full lane with a decision and a loop: no free place above the users, the lane grows by a stripe; the flow nodes keep their columns and rows

daten-ohne.note: two pools; a data object no node uses, named by a lane, top left in that lane; a data store in no lane, top left in its pool; one in the other pool; a text annotation without an association in the process (top left in its pool) and one in the collaboration (above the pools)

daten-namen.note: a long name, a name with a line break and states under them; a data store

daten-weggelassen.note: what stays left out: data associations to a property, to an input of the ioSpecification, to an unknown id, and the data inside a sub-process; the sub-process itself writes a data object
